public.refresh_style_group_counts_batch is declared in claim 2608 and deliberately left untouched. Requirement 4 on issue 2440 is a call-site change, and that function already carries the change predicate from issue 2214. Over-declaring a write is permitted by validateMigrationLease; under-declaring is not.

The reconcile marker is a separate top-level BULK_OPERATIONS key because public.update_bulk_operation (20260819011639) replaces the rebuild-style-groups object wholesale from the caller payload, which would erase a marker stored inside it and destroy the run_id idempotency required by issue 2440 requirement 2.

The advisory lock pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('BULK_OPERATIONS')) is transaction-scoped and is held for the whole reconcile, order 98 seconds once per night, blocking other BULK_OPERATIONS writers for that window. This cost is accepted and documented rather than worked around; releasing it early would reopen the double-fire race the lock closes.

Issue 2440's scope block lists table public.admin_config under reads. The function already writes that table in the baseline body and continues to write exactly the same single row, key = 'BULK_OPERATIONS'. No new table is written. Stated in the migration header and the PR body rather than left to be discovered.

The contract tests require a live database and were NOT executed; no disposable-cluster or preview run is claimed. Their two positive reconcile steps are guarded on the size of public.style_groups so they skip rather than run a full recompute on a production-sized dataset.

The worker-signalled mechanism preferred by the issue author is PopDAM application work in another repository and is not claimed here; nothing in this migration has to be undone to adopt it. Wiring an alert on last_reconciled_at is likewise application work.
